input.spec:
Audit pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/791 (branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2) in repository oakridge. This is an isolated verification run of the committed development definition, not feature work: its only purpose is real analysis, plan, brief, build_result and assessment artifacts for observation to capture and grade. The analysis reports at least three separate findings about this spec, each a distinct observation. Produce exactly one cohort, named audit, with two tasks. T1: a run's launch config carries grading_enabled, off when missing, through the ordered launch delivery (oakridge-dbos/src/domain/run-config.ts, oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation-mapping.ts). T2: settlement of an evaluation execution is fenced to the exact current claim, and completion appends its observation in one transaction (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts, observation/src/grading/worker.ts).
The operator authorizes this audit path: the builder publishes the existing PR #791 as its pr artifact instead of pushing or opening one. No brief may add a further operator choice or confirmation. The builder must not edit files, create commits, push, open or update any pull request, merge, reset a database or deploy. Its worktree starts from epic/grade-pray, the base of pull request #791, so it first checks out the head of branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2 locally (git checkout --detach origin/cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2) and inspects that commit, runs bun install if needed and then bun run --filter observation test once, and publishes build_result with the commit it inspected as head_sha and the actual test counts and output. A test that cannot run is a known issue, never a reason to invent results. It then publishes the existing pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/791 as the pr artifact, with branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2.
The assessor assesses that same commit without changing anything. Give at least one finding per task. Every finding cites at least one file as path:start-end at that commit, for example observation/src/grading/worker.ts:20-40, and cites test output separately as test or output evidence. Report the builder's test run as test_evidence.
Keep the spec, tasks, plan and brief short; there are no ambiguous requirements to resolve.

body.summary: The audit is implementable at local target db2a5d49b8fbcaff9faf03094ddd0757b9c9ecef with exactly the requested T1 and T2. Repository evidence supports default-off grading delivery, exact-claim fencing, and transactional completion. Two non-blocking specification precision gaps remain: ordered delivery is performed in an additional adapter file not named by T1, and the sole mandated observation test run does not execute the focused oakridge-dbos tests for T1.

findings.description: T1 has a concrete source-backed default and validation contract: RunConfig names grading_enabled, parseRunConfig maps absence to false, rejects non-booleans, and returns the parsed value at oakridge-dbos/src/domain/run-config.ts:7-10 and oakridge-dbos/src/domain/run-config.ts:21-41. Focused checked-in cases cover absent, explicit, malformed, and launch-request propagation behavior at oakridge-dbos/tests/run-config.test.ts:56-84.

T1 says ordered launch delivery but names only run-config.ts and observation-mapping.ts. The ordered publisher actually reads the committed launch config, maps it with the event cursor, and posts one acknowledged delivery at oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation.ts:13-20 and oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation.ts:32-46. Omitting this path makes the stated delivery boundary less precise, though no operator decision is needed.

T1 mapping preserves the launch config exactly when committed, emits null when none was committed, and refuses malformed committed config at oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation-mapping.ts:42-48. Focused cases cover enabled, disabled, absent, and malformed mappings at oakridge-dbos/tests/observation-mapping.test.ts:50-65.

T2 exact-claim fencing is explicit: the claim predicate includes claimed status, lease owner, claim attempt, and a database-time unexpired lease; the row is locked before the predicate is re-read and the authoritative update repeats the predicate at observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts:194-228. Stale, reclaimed, old-attempt, and lock-wait expiry cases are checked in observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:304-357.

T2 completion uses one withTenant transaction for the fenced execution update, provider-attempt update, and grade_observation insert at observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts:248-292; the worker passes the exact claim from request marking through completion at observation/src/grading/worker.ts:71-95. The rollback-on-observation-insert-failure case is in observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:231-244.

The required command bun run --filter observation test runs the observation workspace test script defined at observation/package.json:6-8. It can exercise T2 and downstream captured-config behavior, but it does not execute the focused T1 tests under oakridge-dbos/tests/run-config.test.ts:56-84 and oakridge-dbos/tests/observation-mapping.test.ts:50-65. The assessor can still cite inspected test source plus the builder output, but the specification should prevent presenting that output as direct execution of those T1 tests.

Assessor evaluates the same recorded head SHA, emits at least one finding per task, cites commit file ranges and separate builder test/output evidence, and changes nothing.
